title: School Holidays: Maker and Creator - 8 to 12 Years, Darling Square
description: A free two-hour school holiday workshop at Darling Square Library's makerspace where kids aged 8–12 get hands-on with Spheros, Ozobots, Edison robots, wind tubes and LED circuits.
longDescription:
Imagine a school holiday workshop where you walk in as a curious kid and walk out having built a robot, launched something down a wind tube and lit up an LED circuit — all in two hours and completely free. That's exactly what Maker and Creator delivers at the Darling Square Library makerspace, right in the heart of Sydney.

Running throughout the April school holidays, these sessions are designed for kids aged 8–12 who love making things and want to get their hands on technology that usually lives behind glass. The makerspace is packed with the kind of equipment that makes jaws drop, and every session is different — so if you come back twice, you'll try something new both times.

Families can look forward to:
* Free two-hour hands-on sessions in a fully equipped library makerspace
* Robot battles using Edison bots and programmable Sphero and Ozobot challenges
* Wind tube experiments — watch your creations take flight
* LED circuits built with conductive tape — light things up from scratch
* Different activities each session so every visit is a fresh adventure
* Parents and guardians must stay within the library during the session
* Located inside Darling Exchange Building, Haymarket — easy to reach by train
address: 1 Little Pier Street (Level 1–2, Darling Exchange Building), Haymarket NSW 2000
time: 2-hour sessions - check event page for dates
seoTitle: School Holidays Maker and Creator Darling Square | Free Kids STEM Workshop Sydney | Little Discoveries
seoDescription: Free school holiday maker workshop for kids 8–12 at Darling Square Library. Robots, Spheros, Ozobots, wind tubes and LEDs - a hands-on STEM adventure.

title: School Holidays: Creative Coding - Code & Create, 8 to 12 Years
description: A free beginner coding workshop at Darling Square Library where kids aged 8–12 use code to create their own computer-generated printable artwork - no experience needed.
longDescription:
What if your child could use code to make actual, printable art — and take it home at the end? That's the idea behind Creative Coding: Code & Create, a free school holiday workshop at the Darling Square Library Makerspace where kids aged 8–12 discover that coding is as much a creative tool as it is a technical one.

Led by Jared Berghold — a creative coder with over 15 years of experience who has collaborated with artists, galleries and designers around the world — each session is beginner-friendly, hands-on, and genuinely surprising. No prior coding knowledge is needed at all. By the end, every child leaves with a one-of-a-kind piece of computer-generated artwork they created themselves.

Families can look forward to:
* Free beginner-friendly coding workshop with zero experience required
* Learn the fundamentals of creative coding in a fun, accessible way
* Use code to generate unique printable artwork — take it home at the end
* Led by Jared Berghold, an internationally experienced creative coder
* Small group format inside the Darling Square Library Makerspace
* Parents and guardians must remain within the library during the session
* Check the event page for available session dates and times
address: 1 Little Pier Street (Level 1–2, Darling Exchange Building), Haymarket NSW 2000
time: Check event page for session dates and times
seoTitle: School Holidays Creative Coding Darling Square | Free Kids Coding Workshop Sydney | Little Discoveries
seoDescription: Free beginner coding workshop for kids 8–12 at Darling Square Library. Use code to create printable artwork - led by creative coder Jared Berghold.

title: PCYC School Holiday Activities - City of Sydney
description: Safe, fun and affordable full-day school holiday programs for school-aged children at PCYC Woolloomooloo - sport, arts, crafts, coding, laser tag and more. Active and Creative Kids vouchers accepted.
longDescription:
If you're looking for a school holiday program that keeps kids genuinely busy, active and engaged from morning to afternoon, PCYC City of Sydney delivers one of the most well-rounded options in the inner city. Based at their Woolloomooloo centre opposite the Domain Carpark, these full-day and half-day programs for school-aged kids are run by qualified coaches who know how to make sport and activity fun.

The daily schedule mixes sport, arts and creative pursuits so no two afternoons feel the same — and for families who hold Active & Creative Kids vouchers, many activities are eligible for rebates, making this a smart choice for the school holidays. Drop-off from 8am and pick-up until 4pm means it's also genuinely practical for working parents.

Families can look forward to:
* Full-day program running 9:00am–3:00pm with flexible drop-off from 8am and pick-up until 4pm
* Action-packed activities including laser tag, gymnastics, boxing and skateboarding
* Creative options including painting, dance and crafts — something for every kind of kid
* Multi-sport sessions plus coding for tech-interested children
* Delivered by qualified coaches with experience working with young people
* Active and Creative Kids vouchers accepted for eligible activities
* Located at 51 Cathedral Street, Woolloomooloo — close to the city
address: 51 Cathedral Street, Woolloomooloo NSW 2011

title: Tech & Creative Holiday Camps for Ages 5 to 12 - Code Camp
description: Code Camp runs week-long in-person holiday camps for children aged 5–12 covering coding, robotics, stop-motion animation, DJing and more at Sydney locations.
longDescription:
Code Camp has quietly become one of Australia's most popular school holiday programs — and for good reason. These week-long in-person camps turn screen time into skill time, giving kids aged 5–12 the chance to build real projects in coding, robotics, game design and more, guided by experienced instructors who make technology genuinely exciting.

Across multiple Sydney locations, camps run all week with extended hours available at selected venues. Whether your child is into Minecraft, Roblox, robotics or stop-motion film-making, there's a camp track built around their interest. And right now, you can save $25 on any camp booking using the code WOS25 at checkout — making it even better value.

Families can look forward to:
* Week-long immersive camps for children aged 5–12 across multiple tracks
* Minecraft Engineers and Minecraft Minis — build and programme real in-game worlds
* Roblox Legends — design and create games on one of the world's biggest platforms
* Robotics camps — programme physical robots to complete real-world challenges
* Stop-motion animation and DJing camps for creatively-minded kids
* 9:30am–3:30pm daily with extended hours 8am–5pm at selected venues
* Save $25 on your booking with code WOS25 at checkout

title: Ashfield Mall Kids Science Workshops
description: Hands-on science fun for little experimenters! Kids mix, fizz and create their way through experiments like bath bombs, slime, perfumes and lava lamps.
longDescription:
Picture your child's face when they realise they've just made their own lava lamp — and it's actually working. That's a regular moment at the Ashfield Mall Kids Science Workshops, where school holiday sessions are all about hands-on experiments that kids can make, take home, and show off to their friends.

Running Tuesday to Saturday through the school holidays at Ashfield Mall — right opposite Kmart — these popular workshops are run by enthusiastic science educators and cost just $5 per child. They sell out fast, so booking ahead on Eventbrite is essential. The experiments change across sessions, covering everything from chemical reactions and fizzing bath bombs to slime, perfumes and glowing lava lamps.

Families can look forward to:
* Hands-on science experiments kids design, make and take home
* Make fizzing bath bombs and discover the chemistry behind them
* Create their own slime and custom perfume blends
* Build a working lava lamp using everyday materials
* Safe, supervised experiments led by enthusiastic science educators
* Just $5 per child — book ahead on Eventbrite as sessions fill quickly
* Located opposite Kmart inside Ashfield Mall — easy Inner West access
address: Ashfield Mall, Corner of Liverpool Road & Brown Street, Ashfield NSW 2131

title: Featherdale Wildlife Park
description: Get nose-to-nose with wombats, hand-feed kangaroos and spot koalas up close at one of Sydney's best wildlife parks — a guaranteed hit with kids of every age.
longDescription:
Imagine watching your child kneel down and hold out a handful of food, and a kangaroo — a real, full-grown kangaroo — hops right up and eats from their palm. That moment is on offer every single day at Featherdale Wildlife Park in Doonside, and it never gets old no matter how many times you experience it.

Featherdale is home to over 1,700 animals across 260 species, with the emphasis firmly on hands-on encounters rather than distant viewing. Unlike larger, more commercial wildlife parks, Featherdale keeps things intimate and accessible — koalas are close enough to photograph properly, wombats waddle past at ground level, and the keepers are genuinely passionate about sharing what they know. It is consistently voted one of Sydney's best family days out, and the train connection from the city makes it surprisingly easy to reach.

Families can look forward to:
* Hand-feeding kangaroos and wallabies straight from your palm — an unforgettable experience for young children
* Getting genuinely close to koalas, wombats and Tasmanian devils in naturalistic, uncrowded settings
* Walk-through aviaries with native Australian birds swooping overhead
* Reptile encounters including snakes and lizards handled by experienced keepers
* Daily keeper talks and feeding presentations throughout the park
* Easy access by train — Blacktown station, then a short bus or taxi ride
* Open daily 9am–5pm — a full day out from a morning start
address: 217-229 Kildare Road, Doonside NSW 2767
seoTitle: Featherdale Wildlife Park Sydney – Meet Kangaroos, Koalas & More
seoDescription: Hand-feed kangaroos, meet koalas and spot wombats at Featherdale Wildlife Park in Western Sydney. Open daily, great for all ages.

title: Luna Park Sydney
description: Rides, fairy floss and harbour views — Luna Park is Sydney's most iconic family fun destination right on the water at Milsons Point.
longDescription:
There are very few places in Sydney where you can ride a roller coaster with the Sydney Harbour Bridge towering behind you and the Opera House gleaming in the distance. Luna Park on Milsons Point has been making that exact thing possible since 1935 — and nearly a century later, it remains one of the most joyful, photogenic family destinations in Australia.

Park entry is free — you only pay for rides — which makes it a surprisingly flexible outing. You can bring a picnic, sit on the grass with harbour views, and let the kids choose a handful of rides that suit their age and daring. For little ones there are dedicated junior rides; for braver kids and teens there are classic thrillers like the Rotor and the Wild Mouse roller coaster. The landmark Mr Moon face gate is one of the most photographed spots in Sydney, and the whole park carries an irresistible retro charm.

Families can look forward to:
* Free park entry — pay only for the rides you choose, with unlimited ride passes also available
* Classic thrill rides including roller coasters, the Rotor and the Hair Raiser for older kids
* Junior rides and gentle options for toddlers and pre-schoolers — including cars, boats and carousels
* Spectacular views of Sydney Harbour Bridge and Opera House from inside the park
* Fairy floss, popcorn and classic carnival games throughout the grounds
* Open school holidays, weekends and selected weekdays — check the website for current hours
* Arrive by ferry from Circular Quay for a truly memorable harbour approach
address: 1 Olympic Drive, Milsons Point NSW 2061
seoTitle: Luna Park Sydney – Iconic Rides & Harbour Views for the Whole Family
seoDescription: Rides, fairy floss and Sydney Harbour views at Luna Park Milsons Point. Fun for toddlers to teens, open school holidays and weekends.

title: Centennial Parklands – Family Outdoor Fun
description: 580 acres of beautiful parkland in the Eastern Suburbs with playgrounds, cycling, duck ponds, picnic spots and wide open spaces — free to explore any day.
longDescription:
580 acres of parkland, smack in the middle of Sydney's Eastern Suburbs, free to visit every day of the year. Centennial Parklands is the kind of place that becomes a family ritual — the spot you go every Sunday morning, every school holiday, every time you need open air and green space and room to breathe.

The park has something for genuinely every age and energy level. Babies nap in prams along the wide paths while toddlers chase ducks at the ponds. Primary-age kids tear around the playgrounds and beg to hire bikes or pedal cars. Older children explore on foot, spot birds, or bring a ball for a kick in the vast open meadows. And parents get to sit on the grass and do absolutely nothing for an hour, which is also excellent.

Families can look forward to:
* Multiple free playgrounds suited to different age groups — from toddler-safe to big-kid climbing structures
* Feed the ducks, geese and swans at the iconic duck and goose ponds
* Hire bikes, tandems and pedal cars for a leisurely ride around the park (small hire fee)
* Wide open lawns perfect for picnics, cricket, kicking a ball or flying a kite
* Birdwatching — over 130 species recorded in the park, including ibis, herons and parrots
* Café on-site for breakfast and lunch — or BYO and use one of the free BBQ areas
* Open from sunrise to sunset every day — free always, for everyone
address: Centennial Park, Oxford Street, Centennial Park NSW 2021
seoTitle: Centennial Parklands Sydney – Free Family Day Out in the Eastern Suburbs
seoDescription: Free playgrounds, duck ponds, cycling and wide open spaces at Centennial Parklands in Sydney's Eastern Suburbs. Perfect for all ages.

title: Sydney Zoo – Western Sydney's Wild Adventure
description: Come face to face with giraffes, gorillas, hippos and hundreds more animals at Sydney Zoo in Bungarribee Park — a brand new world-class zoo in Western Sydney.
longDescription:
Sydney Zoo opened in Bungarribee Park, Blacktown in 2019 — and in just a few years it has built a reputation as one of Australia's most impressive zoo experiences. Built from scratch on a purpose-designed site, every habitat is larger, more naturalistic and more animal-first than older facilities, which shows in the behaviour and wellbeing of the animals you see.

The headline acts are extraordinary. Giraffes pace through an open African savannah. Western lowland gorillas — one of the world's most endangered great apes — live in a vast forested enclosure. Hippos splash in a river habitat that lets you watch them underwater through floor-to-ceiling glass. Australian wildlife including koalas, wombats and wallabies round out a full day of discovery. With excellent parking, a good café and plenty of shaded seating, it is also one of the most practical family days out in Western Sydney.

Families can look forward to:
* Giraffes roaming an open African savannah — feeding opportunities available on selected days
* Western lowland gorillas in a spacious forested habitat — a genuinely rare encounter
* Watch hippos swimming underwater through panoramic glass viewing panels
* Koalas, wombats, wallabies and Australian reptiles in naturalistic bush settings
* Over 100 species across African, Asian and Australian wildlife zones
* Excellent café, picnic areas and plenty of shaded rest spots throughout the park
* Located next to Eastern Creek with ample free parking — 40 minutes from Sydney CBD
address: Bungarribee Park, Great Western Highway, Blacktown NSW 2148
seoTitle: Sydney Zoo Western Sydney – Giraffes, Gorillas & More at Bungarribee Park
seoDescription: Meet giraffes, gorillas, hippos and over 100 species at Sydney Zoo in Blacktown. A world-class wildlife experience for the whole family.

longDescription:

Whether you're there for the chaos of the Easter Saturday disco or the calm of a weekday Kids Yoga session on the grass, the atmosphere is festive, welcoming and completely free.

The centrepiece of the holidays was the School Holiday Disco on Easter Saturday — with a live DJ set, K-Pop dance classes, a parents' dance-off competition, tumble zone and an Easter Bunny sighting — but the fun rolls on right through until 19 April. Circus shows, roving performers, yoga sessions and play equipment upgrades at Darling Quarter keep families coming back throughout the break.

Families can look forward to:
* Free daily activities across Tumbalong Park with no bookings required
* Easter Saturday Disco with DJ set, K-Pop classes and a parents' dance-off
* Tumble zone with hula hoops, cartwheels and free movement sessions
* Kids Yoga sessions at the Playground Lawn throughout the holidays
* Sync or Swim circus show every Saturday morning
* Roving performers appearing daily across the Darling Harbour precinct
* Refreshed play equipment at Darling Quarter for older kids and tweens

title: Easter School Holidays at Darling Square
description: Free Easter fun for the whole family at Darling Square: egg hunt with prizes, Easter Bunny visits, inflatable jumping castle, face painting, and twisted balloon art.

longDescription:
Darling Square pulls out all the stops for Easter school holidays with a lineup of free activities that make the precinct worth a dedicated visit — or three. Running throughout the NSW Autumn school break (7–17 April 2026), the program is designed for younger children and families who want festive fun without spending a lot.

The Easter egg hunt is the highlight — kids follow clues around the precinct to claim their sweet prize — but the jumping castle, face painting and twisted balloon art mean there's plenty to keep little ones busy well beyond the hunt. With over 50 restaurants and cafes on site, Darling Square is also one of the best spots in the city for a family lunch in between activities.

title: Imagination Station – Space-Themed Activities at Darling Harbour
description: Free drop-in space-themed workshops at Pier Street Underpass: build a rocket, decorate an astronaut mask, design a spaceship, and catch storytimes from Russ the Story Bus. Sensory-friendly.
address: Pier Street Underpass, Darling Harbour, Sydney NSW 2000
longDescription:
The Pier Street Underpass at Darling Harbour has become something remarkable for the April school holidays — Imagination Station, a free all-ages interactive installation where space exploration meets hands-on creativity. It's the kind of place where a five-year-old and a twelve-year-old can both be completely absorbed at the same time, building rockets, decorating astronaut masks and designing spaceships side by side.

The installation runs free as a drop-in all day, every day from 4–19 April, which makes it perfect for a spontaneous visit or a planned adventure. Russ the Story Bus — the travelling library from the Sydney Writers' Festival — pulls up regularly for author storytimes. A giant illustrated art cube by celebrated Australian illustrator James Gulliver Hancock anchors the space and is worth seeing on its own.

Families can look forward to:
* Free drop-in space-themed art and craft activities — no bookings, just turn up
* Build your own rocket from a range of materials and launch it into your imagination
* Decorate an astronaut mask to wear home as a souvenir
* Design and colour your own spaceship — guided by space-age prompts
* Cosmic painting and large-scale collaborative art projects
* Author storytimes aboard Russ the Story Bus — check on-site for timing
* Sensory-friendly activities available throughout — welcoming for all kids
seoTitle: Imagination Station Darling Harbour 2026 – Free Space Activities for Kids | Little Discoveries
seoDescription: Free drop-in space-themed craft and storytimes at Pier Street Underpass, Darling Harbour. Build rockets, decorate astronaut masks and more — no bookings needed.

title: School Holiday Performances & Workshops – Darling Harbour
description: Free weekly shows and workshops at Darling Harbour's Playground Lawn: Rhythm n Bubs music classes on Wednesdays, Sync or Swim circus on Saturdays, Sunday party shows, and Kids Yoga.
address: Darling Harbour, Sydney NSW 2000
longDescription:
Every week of the April school holidays, Darling Harbour's Playground Lawn becomes a stage. Free live performances and workshops run to a weekly schedule from 4–19 April, giving families a reliable reason to keep coming back to one of Sydney's most beautiful outdoor spaces.

The regular highlights are Rhythm n Bubs on Wednesday mornings — a joyful music and movement class led by Phoebe Haselden & Co that has families with babies and toddlers singing and clapping from the first moment — and the Sync or Swim circus show on Saturdays, which is as funny and impressive as it sounds. Sunday mornings bring a Summer Party with Tiptoe Giants. Free Kids Yoga pops up throughout the week between performances.

Families can look forward to:
* Wednesday 10:30–11:15am — Rhythm n Bubs music and movement for babies and toddlers
* Saturday 10:30am and 11:30am — Sync or Swim circus show, outdoors on the lawn
* Sunday 10:30–11:15am — Summer Party show with Tiptoe Giants for all ages
* Free Kids Yoga sessions running throughout the week alongside performances
* Roving performers appearing across the precinct each day without warning
* All events free with no bookings required — arrive a few minutes early for a spot
* Darling Harbour playground and waterfront right next door for play before and after

Move, Groove, Darling brings the energy this school holidays with a free movement festival right at the heart of Darling Harbour. From 13–17 April, Tumbalong Park transforms into an open-air dance and movement space where the whole family can join in, watch, or simply let loose.

Whether your kids are tiny twirlers or teenage hip-hop heads, there is something here for every age and ability. Instructors lead drop-in sessions throughout the day — no bookings, no experience needed, just show up and move.

Families can look forward to:
* Free daily dance workshops including hip-hop, contemporary and family boogie sessions
* Movement and gymnastics circuits for toddlers and pre-schoolers
* Live DJ sets and musical performances across the park

title: Parkoursome – Free Parkour Workshops at Darling Harbour
description: Kids learn real parkour skills from professional coaches at Tumbalong Park — free drop-in sessions all school holidays with jumps, vaults, balance challenges and more.

title: ANZAC Day Dawn Service at Martin Place
description: Sydney's most moving commemoration — the ANZAC Day Dawn Service at Martin Place Cenotaph begins at 4:20am on Saturday 25 April. Free, open to all, and a profound experience for families with older children.
longDescription:
There is something about standing in the dark at 4:20am, surrounded by thousands of Sydneysiders in respectful silence, that stays with children for life. The ANZAC Day Dawn Service at the Martin Place Cenotaph is Australia's most powerful act of community remembrance — and it is completely free and open to everyone.

In 2026, ANZAC Day falls on Saturday 25 April, which means the whole family can attend without worrying about a school night. Crowds begin gathering at the Cenotaph from around 3:30am. The service is brief, solemn and deeply moving — with the Last Post, a minute's silence, and the Rouse. Many families make it an annual tradition, followed by a warm breakfast nearby.

Families can look forward to:
* A profound, moving experience children will remember into adulthood
* The haunting sound of the Last Post echoing through a silent Martin Place
* The first light of dawn breaking over the city during the Rouse
* Free public transport runs through the night for commuters
* Crowds begin gathering from 3:30am — arrive early for a good vantage point
* Combine with a pre-dawn family breakfast afterwards at a nearby cafe
* Broadcast live on free-to-air TV and radio for those who prefer to watch from home

On Saturday 25 April 2026, the March steps off at 9am. Families line the footpaths along Elizabeth Street from as early as 8am to secure a spot. Seeing veterans carry their medals, watching the precision and pride of serving members, and hearing the bands — it is a genuinely moving experience that brings history to life for children far better than any classroom ever could.

longDescription:
The ANZAC Memorial in Hyde Park South is one of Australia's most beautiful and moving buildings — a 1934 Art Deco masterpiece housing the Hall of Memory and the Hall of Service, adorned with sculptures and mosaics that honour the 226,000 NSW men and women who served in the First World War.

On ANZAC Day 2026 (Saturday 25 April), the Memorial runs free 30-minute guided tours every half-hour from 1pm to 4pm. These intimate tours take in the stunning architecture, explain the symbolism built into every detail of the building, and share the human stories of those commemorated. It's a genuinely enriching experience for school-age children and a perfect follow-up to watching the morning march.

Families can look forward to:
* Free 30-minute guided highlights tours — no bookings required, just turn up
* Tours depart from the Hall of Service (Lower Ground Floor) every 30 minutes from 1pm to 4pm
* Learn about the Art Deco design, the sculptures and the powerful symbolism throughout
* Discover individual stories of NSW men and women who served in World War I
* The Pool of Reflection and Hall of Memory are particularly moving spaces for children

longDescription:
Right on the waterfront at Darling Harbour, the Australian National Maritime Museum tells the remarkable story of Australia's relationship with the sea — and on ANZAC Day, that story is particularly poignant. The museum holds significant naval history from Gallipoli to the Pacific, from Kokoda to the present day, and ANZAC Day brings special programming that brings these stories to life.

The main museum galleries are free to enter, covering everything from Indigenous sea voyaging to the First Fleet, convict transportation, naval warfare and modern maritime adventure. These vessels carry an entry fee but the museum itself is free — making this an outstanding family day out.

title: ANZAC Memorial Hyde Park – Free Sunday Guided Tour
description: A free one-hour guided tour of the ANZAC Memorial in Hyde Park every Sunday at 10am — explore the stunning 1934 Art Deco architecture and hear the moving stories behind one of Sydney's most significant buildings.
longDescription:
If your family missed the ANZAC Day special tours on Saturday, the ANZAC Memorial offers its regular free guided tours every Sunday at 10am — and they are just as worthwhile any week of the year.

The memorial is a 1934 Art Deco masterpiece that honours the 226,000 men and women of NSW who served in the First World War. The hour-long highlights tour takes in the Hall of Memory and Hall of Service, explains the extraordinary symbolism built into the architecture, the sculptures by Rayner Hoff, and the thousands of names inscribed throughout the building. It is quietly magnificent — and children who've just watched the ANZAC Day march the day before will find the stories particularly resonant.

Families can look forward to:
* Free one-hour guided highlights tour every Sunday at 10am — no bookings needed
* Explore the stunning Art Deco architecture of one of Australia's finest memorials
* Discover the stories of NSW men and women commemorated within the building
* The Hall of Memory's domed ceiling and the Pool of Reflection are breathtaking
* Sculptures by renowned Australian artist Rayner Hoff throughout the building
* Open 9am–5pm daily with free entry — worth exploring independently too
* Located in Hyde Park South — combine with a picnic in the park afterwards
address: Hyde Park South, Liverpool Street, Sydney NSW 2000
costLabel: free entry and free guided tour

title: Art Gallery NSW – Free Family Sunday Visit
description: The Art Gallery of NSW is free to visit every day — on Sunday 26 April, combine free general admission with weekend family art-making activities, roving gallery educators and a picnic in the Domain.
longDescription:
The Art Gallery of New South Wales is one of Australia's finest cultural institutions — and one of its most generous, with free general admission always. Sunday 26 April is the perfect day to visit: the post-ANZAC-Day long weekend means the city is quieter than usual, and the gallery's weekend family programs are in full swing.

Across the two buildings — the classical heritage wing and the spectacular new Sydney Modern building — families can explore everything from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art to European masters, contemporary Australian works and striking photography. Weekend roving activities see gallery educators pop up with art-making materials inspired by works on display. The Domain parkland outside is perfect for a post-gallery picnic.

Families can look forward to:
* Free general admission to both the heritage building and Sydney Modern — always
* Weekend family art-making activities with roving gallery educators
* The stunning Sydney Modern building with spectacular harbour views from the roof terrace
* Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander galleries — one of the finest collections in Australia
* The Domain parkland right outside — perfect for a family picnic after the gallery
* Café and restaurant in both buildings for a relaxed family lunch
* Easy access via St James, Museum or Martin Place train stations
address: Art Gallery Road, The Domain, Sydney NSW 2000
venue: Art Gallery of New South Wales
